subject: Recap and next ops: embeddings + streaming pilot feasibility
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Liang <emma@vectorly.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@vectorly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap and next ops: embeddings + streaming pilot feasibility

Hi Emma / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to understand where Vectorly is headed with contextual search and live session ranking. Quick recap from our side and proposed next ops so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search quality drops for long-tail product docs and ephemeral session context (user state not persisted cleanly).
- High per-request cost when doing dense re-ranking over long histories; want predictable unit economics.
- Need sub-200ms 95th percentile for interactive session reranking in the web UI.

Goals you want from the pilot:
1) Improve relevance for session-aware ranking using streaming embeddings + lightweight rerank.
2) Validate latency SLOs under typical QA traffic (50 r/s burst, 10 concurrent sessions).
3) Quantify cost delta vs current hosted vectors + CPU rerank approach.

Proposed pilot approach (high level):
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week setup + 2-week load/quality evaluation).
- Components: Redwood hosted embedding endpoint (quantized model), streaming token-level scoring for live sessions (low-latency path), and a reranker running on a cheap GPU-backed Dedicated pool for candidate reorders.
- Integration footprint: small SDK change to use our streaming function-calling hook for incremental scores + a backfill job for historical vectors. We’ll provide a one-file reference example that fits into your current client.

Open technical constraints we flagged that need confirmation from you:
- Data residency: will Vectorly require EU-only hosting for any pilot data?
- Sample rate: do you have a limit on sending every keystroke vs periodic snapshots (we recommend periodic snapshots every 2–3s to balance cost and signal).
- Candidate set size for the reranker (we assumed 50 candidates).

Attachments: I attached a short pilot scope workbook and an architecture diagram that shows the streaming function-call path and where embedding caching happens. There’s also a small mock dataset you can use for the initial smoke tests.

Immediate next steps
- Emma: confirm data residency and whether we should provision EU-only resources (reply by Wed 8/2).
- Vectorly: share a representative sample of session events (anonymized) — we’ll validate schema compatibility.
- Redwood: we’ll draft a one-page SOW and provide a reference SDK snippet for streaming function-calls by Tue 8/3.

If that looks right I’ll open a HubSpot deal stage for Pilot > Prepare and loop in our solutions engineer for the kickoff.

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-emb-pilot-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet), streaming-funcall-constraints-arch-diagram.pdf (pdf), pilot-mock-data-sample.jsonl (sample)

From: Emma Liang <emma@vectorly.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@vectorly.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next ops: embeddings + streaming pilot feasibility

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: for the pilot we prefer US region but we will need EU-only for production. US is fine for the short trial.
- Keystroke sampling: we currently batch events every ~3s on the client, so that matches your recommendation.
- Candidate set: 50 sounds reasonable to start.

A couple of technical questions before you draft the SOW: 
1) SDK changes — how invasive is the streaming function-call change? We’d like to avoid a large refactor on the front end. Can you share the reference snippet now (even a pseudo-code block)?
2) Embedding model ops — will you provide an on-the-fly quantized model endpoint, or do we push vectors to your service? We need to understand the network egress pattern for cost modeling.

We’ll assemble an anonymized sample and share a link by Tue. If you can send the SDK example and a delta-cost estimate (rough) that’d help us prepare the internal approval.

—Emma
Emma Liang
Head of ML Engineering | Vectorly
emma@vectorly.ai

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the quick confirmations. Attached is a tiny SDK snippet (JS pseudo) and a very rough cost-delta note — both are attached inline below and I’ve also uploaded the same to the Drive link. High-level answers: 

- SDK impact: minimal. The streaming function-call path is an opt-in shim. Your front-end only needs to call the new client.streamSessionScores(sessionId, events, callback) method instead of the current batch inference call; the old path remains available for fallbacks. I included a JS snippet in the attachment.
- Embedding endpoint: we’ll host a quantized endpoint and support push ingestion. For the pilot we recommend push-ingested vectors for stable historical context and streaming for live updates — that minimizes egress and gives us better cache hit rates.

Attached items (also in Drive):
- redwood-sdk-streaming-snippet.js (2-file example)
- redwood-cost-delta-estimate.pdf (very rough numbers; final will depend on sample you provide)
- pilot-sow-draft.docx (1-page SOW)

Next steps re-confirmed:
- Vectorly to share anonymized sample by Tue 9/2 EOD.
- Redwood to provision temporary Dedicated A10 on Wed 9/3 for initial load smoke.
- Jordan to schedule 30m kickoff with engineering (Proposed: Thu 9/4 11am PT) — I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm availability.

If anything is missing or you want the SOW tweaked (timeline or deliverables) say so and we’ll update. Looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
